chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Indeed, Allah, Glorified is He, made obedience a prize for the intelligent when the disabled fall short.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that obedience is a prize for the intelligent when the disabled fall short?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of 'booty' (ghanimah' (war booty) to illustrate that obedience is a prize reserved for the intelligent who actively compensate for the deficiencies of the weak. This highlights the Shia concept of 'ta'ah' not merely as individual duty, but as a dynamic social responsibility where the capable elevate the collective spiritual status by covering the gaps left by those unable to fulfill obligations fully. It underscores the merit of compensatory worship (kaffarat al-nuqshan) in Islamic jurisprudence and ethics.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 331. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
When the disabled fall short in performing acts of obedience to Allāh, the Glorified, it is a good opportunity given by Allāh for the intelligent to perform such acts.
